parole.testo: Via a Turkic language, ultimately from Middle Mongol 札撒兀勒 (zhásāwùlè /⁠⁠ǰasa'ul⁠/). Compare Ukrainian осавул (osavul, “Cossack captain”). Distantly related to яса́к (jasák).
From a Turkic language, ultimately from Middle Mongol *ïrgaï. Compare Kazakh ырғай (ırğay, “juneberry”), Mongolian яргай (jargaj, “dogwood, cornel”).
From a Turkic language, ultimately from Middle Mongol 合班; Compare Kazakh қабан (qaban), Tatar кабан (qaban), Azerbaijani qaban, Turkish kaban (dialectal) and others.
A Turkic borrowing; compare Tatar каравыл (qarawıl), Kazakh қарауыл (qarawıl). Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯ (qaraɣul).
Borrowed from a Turkic language. Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠰᠠᠭᠠᠳᠠᠭ (saɣadaɣ, “quiver”); see Azerbaijani sadaq and Bashkir һаҙаҡ (haðaq) for more.

parole.significato: driver, coachman, charioteer, cabman, postilion engaged in transporting people and cargo by horse and carriage
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic ямьщикъ (jamĭščikŭ), from Turkic. Compare Tatar ямчы (yamçı), Turkish yamçı. Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠵᠠᠮᠴᠢ (ǰamči) (see Mongolian зам (zam)). Ending modified under the influence of -щик (-ščik).
From Turkic, from Middle Mongol ᠵᠠᠰᠠᠭ (ǰasaɣ). Compare Tatar ясак (yasaq), Turkish yasak. Related to есау́л (jesaúl).
